final_text:
Job J-2240 was not released. 0 of 3 panels have a passing QC record.

2240-1 failed QC: DFT at the five points was 0–38 µm (limits 60–90) and the camera recorded runs. Those runs came from an early trial coat that went on too wet; runs cannot be repaired in the booth, so that panel cannot pass on a later check.

2240-2 and 2240-3 each got one full coat at standoff 100 mm, 250 ml/min, 400 mm/s, pitch 40 mm, margin 20 mm (about 93 ml each, no sag). Robot time expired before the 60 s flash-off, so they were never measured or QC’d. From card and panel trials, that coat should be only about 25 µm DFT.

Process limit found during the test: at the closest allowed standoff (100 mm, best transfer of the settings tried), dry film is only about 9% of the wet film you would calculate from pot volume divided by area. A single coat much above ~300 µm wet-equivalent sags and runs. Staying under that limit and waiting more than 90 s between coats can stack film without runs, but even the full 470 ml pot, with no waste, only supports about 45–50 µm average DFT on all three panels — short of 60 µm. Time ran out before a multi-coat plan could be finished.

I would not run SB-2 unattended on this job until pot volume, transfer, and the 60–90 µm spec are reconciled. Do not ship J-2240.
